findings.claim: In getAuthorizationConditions for org scope, userIdsFromOrg is fetched only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. For orgs with no child teams, org-level members' personal bookings are excluded, even though teamIds already includes orgId.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:157-162 only calls MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, although teamIds at line 154 already contains options.orgId; with no child teams userIdsFromOrg is [] and the `isTeamBooking = false` branch at lines 166-169 is skipped, so org members' personal bookings are left out. The guard sits in unchanged context lines of the patch hunk (@@ -159,31 +161,22), which only rewrote the return into raw SQL.

findings.claim: The integration tests for team and org scope conditions only compare the generated Prisma.Sql structure with toEqual and never run the queries against Postgres. The ANY(...) array-parameter binding paths are therefore untested at runtime.

verifier.reason: The team and org scope tests only assert `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...ANY(${[...]})...`)` (packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:294-299, 330-343). The only test that executes SQL via `prisma.$queryRaw` uses `scope: "user"` with no ANY(...) (same file, lines 468-484), and no other test file exercises InsightsBookingService.

findings.claim: The hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type flattens the zod discriminated union and makes teamId optional for all scopes. A team-scope call without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at runtime and silently returns empty results; this is also inconsistent with InsightsRoutingService's strict union type.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34 adds a flat type with `teamId?: number` and the constructor accepts it at :58, so `{scope:"team"}` without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at :62-63 (options = null) and yields `1=0` at :126-127, i.e. silently empty results; InsightsRoutingService still takes the strict z.infer union at insightsRouting.ts:29,52. The only current callers are the integration tests, so nothing hits this path today.

findings.claim: The test fixtures userEventType and userBooking are cleaned up only after the assertions, not in try/finally. A failing query or expectation leaves those rows in the integration database.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:445-466 the test creates userEventType and userBooking, and the only cleanup is the inline deletes at lines 494-500 after the raw query (481-484) and the expect (487-491), with no try/finally or afterEach, so a throw from either skips the deletes. The create/cleanup structure is unchanged context in the patch (only the query and assertion at patch lines 254-273 changed), so it predates this change.

findings.claim: In getBaseConditions(), the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a truthy Prisma.Sql.

verifier.reason: Every return path of buildAuthorizationConditions() yields a Prisma.Sql object (packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:125-142, with the org/team helpers reducing over non-empty arrays at :164-174 and :196-207), and getAuthorizationConditions() is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> (:83-88). So `authConditions` is always truthy and the `else if (filterConditions)` / `else` branches at :76-80 can never run.

findings.claim: The org-scope test assertion depends on the order of ids inside ANY(...) arrays. Those ids come from repository queries (findAllByParentId, MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds) without orderBy, so the SQL-fragment equality is nondeterministic.

verifier.reason: The org-scope assertion at packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332-343 compares ANY(...) arrays in a fixed order, while the ids come from findMany calls with no orderBy (packages/lib/server/repository/team.ts:192-197, packages/lib/server/repository/membership.ts:409-419) and are used unsorted at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:154-168. The pre-patch assertion had the same order dependence through `in: [...]` arrays, and Postgres will usually return insertion order here, so this is a latent flake rather than an observed failure.

findings.claim: The 'Caching' describe block test was deleted, but the memoisation code it covered (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions) remains and is now untested.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the whole `describe("Caching")` block from packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts (old lines ~473-547), leaving only the Authorization Conditions, Filter Conditions and getBaseConditions blocks (lines 202, 349, 437), while the memoisation remains at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:84-94 with no test calling either getter twice. The deleted tests only compared two calls with `toEqual`, so they would have passed without caching anyway.

findings.claim: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition produce top-level OR expressions without outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions() returns them directly. When callers compose them with AND, operator precedence lets rows matching the first OR branch bypass additional filters.

verifier.reason: The org/team builders return a bare `(A) OR (B)` (packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:171-174, 204-207), and getBaseConditions() returns it unwrapped when there are no filters (insightsBooking.ts:74-75), so appending `AND ...` to it would bind only to the second OR branch. The risk is latent: with filters present line 73 parenthesises correctly, and the only current caller (the integration test, line 480) uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` alone.

findings.claim: The same AND/OR reduce fold is hand-written three times instead of using Prisma.join or a direct expression.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:119-122 (AND), :171-174 (OR) and :204-207 (OR) each hand-write the same `conditions.reduce((acc, condition, index) => index === 0 ? condition : Prisma.sql`(acc) OP (condition)`)` fold, and the file uses no Prisma.join or shared helper. All three are lines added by the patch.
